TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - complete lymphocyte depletion achieved with lymphocyte count dropping to 0.0065 K/uL at day 0, demonstrating successful targeting of autoreactive lymphocytes. CD19+ B cells and CD3+/CD4+/CD8+ T cells were depleted as intended. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear evidence of downstream pathway modulation - immune reconstitution occurred with gradual recovery of depleted cell populations, indicating the mechanism of lymphocyte depletion followed by immune system reset was engaged. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with median relapse-free complete clinical response of 54 months. Disease activity biomarkers improved dramatically: SLEDAI score decreased from 4.25 to 0, anti-dsDNA antibodies decreased from 17.3 to 0 IU, and ANA decreased from 5.4 to 2.5 EU. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported, but the severe SLE population showed robust response. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm trial with small sample size (n=9) limits interpretation, but the magnitude and duration of response (54 months median) with complete biomarker normalization suggests genuine efficacy beyond natural fluctuation.

failure_modes.evidence: Small sample size of 9 patients limits statistical power and generalizability, though the magnitude of response suggests real efficacy
